components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 50px; padding: 14px 18px; border: 0; border-radius: 13px; color: #fff; background: #28669f; font: 700 14px/1.4 'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 7px 16px #28669f20; transition: transform 170ms ease, background 170ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1d4f7c; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #3e7fb7; outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(.98); }

narrative.overview: Tracky pairs an in-development React component library with an analytics SDK for developers who want useful product signals while keeping control of where those signals go. Its interface should feel precise, open, and trustworthy. Soft blue marks the event path and active choices. White space keeps the page readable. A routing diagram and a clearly labeled component preview show the intended product without implying the library is shipped or hosted infrastructure exists.
keyCharacteristics: Blue routing lines connect a component layer, SDK, and developer endpoint.
Plus Jakarta Sans gives headings and body copy one consistent voice.
Dark, restrained code and signal panels distinguish implementation examples from marketing copy.
dos: Do make the configured endpoint and developer-owned data path clear.
Do label example data, the component preview, and animated route behavior as illustrative.
Do keep opt-in capture and privacy boundaries accurate to the product implementation.
donts: Don't imply Tracky provides a collector, dashboard, durable queue, consent manager, or guaranteed delivery.
Don't add gradients, generic feature-card grids, or unsupported performance claims.
